To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PMPA is an effective antiretrovirus drug for the treatment and prevention of HIV infection.
PMPA is an effective antiretrovirus agent that can prevent the establishment of persistent SIV infection in macauges when treatment is started within 24 h after virus exposure.

(i) PMPA treatment initiated within the first 24 h after virus inoculation prevents establishment of persistent infection; (ii) PMPA is effective in preventing establishment of infection even when treatment is initiated 48 h after inoculation, but not when it is initiated 72 h after inoculation; and (iii) the duration of PMPA therapy is a crucial factor for protection.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the efficacy of PMPA for preventing acute SIV infection depends critically on the time to initiation and duration of treatment, and that even a short delay in the initiation of treatment or shortening of the treatment duration can result in a dramatic reduction in the efficacy of this agent for prevention of persistent SIV infection in macaues.

PMPA is effective in preventing SIV infection in cynomolgus monkeys, but the timing of treatment is very important.
the time between virus inoculation and the initiation of antiviral treatment, and the duration of treatment, are critical factors for preventing establishment of persistent HIV-1 or SIV infection.
